producer_report.summary: Moved the Early pull request and CI wait row from gh/mod.rs into new gh/early.rs. The function and struct text is unchanged except the visibility keywords listed below. gh/mod.rs declares `mod early;`, re-exports EARLY_RUN_WAIT, EarlyPr and open_early_pr, and imports replace_early and wait_for_checks for land_pr and publish. I did not run the full `cargo test --locked`, left to Athena's checks.

open_issues: The full `cargo test --locked` was not run by me (left to Athena). I ran `cargo test --locked -- --list` but did not diff it against a base list. The 75 gh tests and the policy scan pass.
I did not inspect the single bare-name hit in run_pin_tests.rs.
mistakes: I first wrote `super::early_seam::current()` in early.rs, which changed one line of moved text. I reverted it to `early_seam::current()` and added a cfg(test) import instead.
learnings: Caller check per moved name (grep across crates/): EARLY_RUN_WAIT is used by gh/client.rs through `super::EARLY_RUN_WAIT`, which the re-export satisfies. EarlyPr and open_early_pr are used by Athena::early_pr_to (now in early.rs) and by gh/mod.rs tests via `use super::*`; run_pin_tests.rs matched the bare-name grep once, but its hit was not inspected. EARLY_RUN_JOB is used only by mod.rs tests (hence pub(super) plus a `#[cfg(test)]` import). EARLY_RUN_STEP, wait_for_early_run, name_failure, https_github_repository and early_pr_to are used only inside early.rs. replace_early is used by land_pr and publish in mod.rs. wait_for_checks is used by land_pr in mod.rs, which reads Waited's three fields. Athena::early_pr is called from run/mod.rs (`self.early_pr(...)`) and its path is unchanged.
The early_seam test module stays in mod.rs because it was not in the row; early.rs reaches it through `#[cfg(test)] use super::early_seam;`, so the moved text is unchanged.
After the move mod.rs no longer used ReplaceRequest, check_replace or store_early_link. load_early_link and store_early are now used only by tests, so they are imported under `#[cfg(test)]`.
`cargo test --locked -- --list` output is large and includes compile noise, so a diff against the base list needs the base run too.
desires: A command to extract a line range of a file would let me move text without retyping it. Retyping is where a copy slip could enter.
